title: Exchange rates and the balance of payments
summary: Exchange rates are set by demand and supply of currencies, or fixed or managed by governments. Their movements affect trade, inflation and growth. The balance of payments records all transactions with the rest of the world. HL adds conversions, the Marshall–Lerner condition, the J-curve and the terms of trade.

keyterms.definition: The price of one currency in terms of another.
An exchange rate determined by market demand and supply without government intervention.
An exchange rate set and maintained by the government or central bank against another currency.
A floating rate where the central bank intervenes periodically to influence its value.
A rise in the value of a currency in a floating system.
A fall in the value of a currency in a floating system.
A deliberate reduction in the value of a fixed exchange rate by the government.
A record of all transactions between residents of a country and the rest of the world over a period.
Records trade in goods and services, primary income (wages, interest, profits) and secondary income (transfers).
Records capital transfers and the sale or purchase of non-produced, non-financial assets.
Records direct investment, portfolio investment and changes in reserve assets.
When the debits (e.g. imports) on the current account exceed the credits; it must be matched by a surplus on the capital and financial accounts.
A depreciation improves the current account only if the sum of the PEDs for exports and imports is greater than 1.
The path of the current account after a depreciation: it worsens at first (inelastic demand in the short run) then improves.
Index of average export prices ÷ index of average import prices × 100.

questions.prompt: Which would cause the euro to appreciate against the dollar?
options: Higher interest rates in the eurozone attracting US savings
Eurozone residents buying more US goods
questions.explanation: Demand for euros rises as investors seek higher returns.

questions.statement: A depreciation of a country’s currency makes its exports cheaper for foreigners.
questions.explanation: Foreign buyers need less of their currency to buy the same goods.

questions.text: A deliberate cut in the value of a fixed exchange rate is a ___.
questions.explanation: Depreciation is the floating-rate equivalent.

questions.prompt: Match each event to its effect on the domestic currency (floating).
questions.explanation: Anything raising demand for the currency raises its value; anything raising supply lowers it.

questions.prompt: Which is a likely consequence of a strong appreciation?
questions.explanation: Cheaper imports reduce inflation, but exporters lose competitiveness.

questions.prompt: How does a central bank keep a fixed exchange rate from falling?
options: It buys its own currency using foreign reserves or raises interest rates
questions.explanation: Buying the currency increases demand for it.

questions.statement: A floating exchange rate gives a country freedom to use monetary policy for domestic goals.
questions.explanation: It does not need interest rates to defend a currency peg.

questions.text: A floating rate with occasional central bank intervention is a ___ exchange rate.
questions.explanation: Many countries operate managed floats.

questions.prompt: Which is an advantage of a fixed exchange rate?
questions.explanation: Stable rates reduce exchange-rate risk.

questions.prompt: Order the effect of a fall in domestic interest rates on the exchange rate.
items: Hot money flows out of the country
questions.explanation: Interest rate differentials drive short-term capital flows.

questions.prompt: Where are profits earned by foreign-owned firms and sent home recorded?
options: Primary income in the current account
questions.explanation: Investment income is primary income.

questions.prompt: Match each transaction to its account.
questions.explanation: The BoP has three accounts plus errors and omissions.

questions.statement: A current account deficit must be matched by a surplus on the capital and financial accounts.
questions.explanation: Overall the BoP balances, apart from errors and omissions.

questions.text: Foreign direct investment is recorded in the ___ account.
questions.explanation: FDI and portfolio investment are financial account items.

questions.prompt: Which is a possible consequence of a persistent current account deficit?
options: Rising foreign debt or sale of domestic assets to foreigners
questions.explanation: The deficit must be financed by borrowing or selling assets.

questions.prompt: Which policy aims to reduce a current account deficit through expenditure reduction?
options: Contractionary fiscal policy to reduce spending on imports
questions.explanation: Lower incomes reduce import spending; expenditure switching uses tariffs or depreciation.

questions.statement: Supply-side policies that improve competitiveness can reduce a current account deficit in the long run.
questions.explanation: Higher productivity makes exports more competitive.

questions.text: A record of all transactions with the rest of the world is the balance of ___.
questions.explanation: The balance of trade is only part of the current account.

questions.prompt: A large current account surplus may cause…
options: upward pressure on the exchange rate and friction with trading partners
questions.explanation: Strong demand for exports raises demand for the currency.

questions.prompt: Order the sections of the balance of payments as usually presented.
questions.explanation: The sum of all should be zero.

lessons.title: HL: Conversions, Marshall–Lerner, J-curve and terms of trade

questions.prompt: €1 = $1.25. How many euros is a $50 item?
Goods balance −40, services +15, primary income −5, secondary income +10 (all $ bn). What is the current account balance?

questions.statement: The Marshall–Lerner condition says a depreciation improves the current account if PEDx + PEDm > 1.
questions.explanation: Demand must be elastic enough for volumes to outweigh the price changes.

questions.prompt: Why does the current account often worsen immediately after a depreciation?
options: Demand for exports and imports is inelastic in the short run
questions.explanation: Contracts and habits take time to change: the J-curve effect.

questions.prompt: The export price index rises to 110 and the import price index to 125. What are the terms of trade?
questions.explanation: 110 ÷ 125 × 100 = 88: a deterioration.

questions.statement: An improvement in the terms of trade means each unit of exports buys more imports.
questions.explanation: Export prices rise relative to import prices.

questions.text: The path of the current account after a depreciation (worse, then better) is the ___-curve.
questions.explanation: Shown as a J on a graph of the balance over time.

questions.prompt: Match each cause to its effect on the terms of trade.

pairs.right: Improves: exports dearer in foreign currency

questions.explanation: Anything raising export prices relative to import prices improves the ToT.

questions.prompt: Order the J-curve following a depreciation.
items: Import bill rises as volumes adjust slowly
Volumes respond and the balance improves
questions.explanation: Over time, demand becomes more elastic and Marshall–Lerner holds.
